hook: A nanofiber scaffold lets stacked perovskite layers form large, tough films that detect x-rays well.
summary: Researchers used an electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber mesh as a scaffold to build freestanding perovskite films, over 99 wt% perovskite, in layers of different compositions. The mesh also passivates defects at interfaces. A 2D/3D film made this way detected x-rays below the medical standard limit. The demonstration is one device type, and long-term stability is not described.
title: Chemically Anchored Rebar Perovskites for Deterministic Layer-by-Layer Integration.
